messages:
deploy-bot: [ALERT] node algos-rt-12 OOMKilled (container=serving-runtime) x3 in 5m - pod restart flurry
oncall-sre: seeing same on algos-rt-11 and -12, memory climbs slowly then spike OOM, CUDA errors in kernel log right before crash :grimacing:
eng-runtime-bot: metrics: kv_cache_resident_bytes on algos-rt-11 -> +18% over 30m, slab fragmentation rising, page-faults up 3x
marta: probable paged-attention allocator slow-creep. last week we saw similar but lower rate. suspect KV cache fragmentation -> inability to satisfy large seq allocations -> oom path
samir: can we confirm kvcache eviction is running? i see eviction throughput drop around 13:12UTC in traces
oncall-sre: eviction loop still scheduled but stalling on compaction step, logs show repeated "compaction skipped: no contiguous pages" entries. patching compaction isn't immediate
kevin: cust-ops says a handful of customers hit 502s and model timeouts this morning. low volume but persistent for 12m. ticket #C-8042 opened
lia: suggested quick mitigations: 1) reduce KV_CACHE_MAX_BYTES on affected nodes to force early evictions, 2) enable emergency_compaction toggle, 3) cordon & rotate node if compaction can't free enough
ryan: +1 to cordon/rotate. also consider routing policy -> fallback to quantized-smaller variant (model: redwood-small-q4) for sessions on these nodes to reduce KV pressure
marta: commands i propose:```
# limit kvcache on node
kubectl -n infra patch daemonset serving-runtime -p '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"containers":[{"name":"serving","env":[{"name":"KV_CACHE_MAX_BYTES","value":"17179869184"}]}]}}}}'
# enable emergency compaction via runtime flag
kubectl exec -n infra -it pod/serving-runtime-ctrl -- /bin/sh -c 'echo 1 > /sys/fs/serving/emergency_compaction'
```
oncall-sre: applying KV_CACHE_MAX_BYTES patch to algos-rt pool now, rolling restart set to 30s between pods. starting with algos-rt-12 (most noisy)
eng-runtime-bot: deploy job started by oncall-sre @ 6161616180 - rollout 3/12 pods updated
samir: while rollout runs, can infra spin up 2 extra algos-rt nodes in the pool? short-term scale-out reduces per-node pressure and gives time for compaction to work
lia: infra asked to add 2 nodes, ETA ~4m. cordoning algos-rt-12 after pods evicted
kevin: cust-ops: informing affected customers we're investigating, providing ETA 20-30m and workaround of retrying requests; no broad outage, limited impact :white_check_mark:
marta: if compaction fails, we should enable node-level memory overcommit guard: set SERVING_HEAP_GUARD=0.85 to trigger earlier throttles and avoid hard OOMs (will increase tail latency though)
oncall-sre: emergency compaction toggled on algos-rt-12, starting manual compaction trigger now: `/usr/local/bin/serving-ctl compact --force`
eng-runtime-bot: manual compaction run completed on algos-rt-12: freed ~7.2GB, fragmentation down 12%
ryan: good, continue rollout, but also start routing-policy change: move new requests away from algos-rt-11/12 -> warm pool alt-region until stabilized
lia: routing change applied: traffic diverted, 10% of sessions moved to fallback pool, 90% normal.
oncall-sre: algos-rt-12 restarted cleanly, memory climb slowed. algos-rt-11 still showing slow creep, scheduling step for 11 now
samir: logs show occasional CUDA driver WARNs before crash: "CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS" - could be triggered by fragmented allocations crossing page boundaries
marta: note for postmortem: allocator needs compaction heuristics for long-lived KV patterns (pinning small fragments). put task on eng-runtime backlog: add async background compaction heuristics and a diagnostic to mark hot KV slots
kevin: customer impact update: two customers saw transient 502 spikes for ~15m, both auto-recovered after retries. cust-ops closed advisory with workaround info. no escalations
oncall-sre: summary: actions taken -> limited traffic routing, KV limit patch rolled, emergency compaction, cordon/rotate noisy node, scale-out +2 nodes. immediate severity reduced. followups: postmortem runbook update, add alert for compaction_skipped logs, and longer-term allocator work (marta + samir)
marta: creating incident ticket INT-2026-314, will add timeline and assign owners. adding reproducer steps for local perf env
ryan: leaving note to ops: if you see recurrent CUDA_ILLEGAL errors after defragmentation, do full node reboot (not just pod restart) to clear driver-state
oncall-sre: thanks all — monitoring for 30m, will update if anything changes :thumbsup:
